items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: That's why he made them records with Lewis, you know what I mean? The Kid Oren and Hot Fire.

ctx.x: So he played around here, wasn't he? This is home, yeah, sure. He played too.

Who did George play with? Who did George play with? Who did George? Foster. Who George? George played all different man with Kid Punch. Last time he left and he played with Kid Punch. Yeah, with Punch. George left and he went to New York, not New York, Chicago. That's why he made them records with Lewis, you know what I mean? The Kid Oren and Hot Fire. George Foster. He be jeezing all that thing, you know what I mean? He made all that stuff, you know what I mean? Muscat Rambles. George and all that recording.
Did you play with a brass band in different range? No. Did you ever play with any brass bands here in the city?

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: King, you remember we played with Lou's Armstrong?

ctx.x: You can know Poe Dee's style. Poe is a brass band. You talk about a brass band. I'm not saying that because he's here.
King, King, be with me, King. Listen, we'll be laughing. I have to worry. King, you remember we played with Lou's Armstrong? What was he close to Walk with Dee? Is he in D flat?
No, that was the saint. The grand finale.
